https://www.berlinale.de/en/2011/program.note: Alexander/Aleksandr Mindadze are transliterations of the same director. Official Berlinale uses Alexander; Norwegian film-club federation credits Aleksandr for the same Chernobyl film.

The official original title and longer English alias correspond to the international release title A Separation. Discover through the verified IMDb identity, then retain exact title/director/year checks. Cineart distributor pressbook confirms Farhadi, 2011 and 123 minutes.

https://www.berlinale.de/en/2012/program.note: Bence is the familiar form of Benedek Fliegauf. Hungarian National Film Institute uses Bence in its film description and Benedek in its on-set photograph credit for Just the Wind.

Brillante Mendoza / Brillante Ma Mendoza / Brillante Ma. Mendoza are director-name variants. Sales agent Playtime explicitly credits Brillante Ma Mendoza for Captive (2012); Unifrance pressbook credits Brillante Ma. Mendoza. Official archive production year 2011 and 2012 festival/release year are compatible.
The official archive abbreviates the repeated surname as Paolo & Vittorio Taviani. Filmitalia and Karlovy Vary separately credit both directors for Caesar Must Die.

https://www.berlinale.de/en/2013/program.note: Malgoska/Małgośka and Małgorzata are documented forms of the same director name, explicitly cross-referenced by Filmportal. Other official festival sources connect both variants to In the Name Of.

The Necessary Death of Charlie Countryman was released as Charlie Countryman. AFI credits Fredrik Bond and 2013 for that film; IMDb retains the longer original title. Use verified IMDb discovery and short-title alias, preserving exact director/title checks.

Kamboziya/Kambuzia Partovi is a transliteration variant; both directors remain required. IFC Center separately credits Jafar Panahi and Kambuzia Partovi for Closed Curtain, while Berlinale uses Kamboziya.

https://www.berlinale.de/en/2015/program.note: Generic Body searches omitted the 2015 Polish feature. Verified IMDb discovery identifies Małgorzata Szumowska’s film, also distributed as Body/Ciało. Official Polish distributor Kino Świat confirms title, director and year.
Alexey/Aleksei is a transliteration variant of German Jr. Film at Lincoln Center credits Aleksei for Under Electric Clouds, while the official Berlinale and sales agent Films Boutique use Alexey.
